# Releases
## ai@7.0.173

### Patch Changes

- f43ee39: fix(workflow): log the default step limit warning when
`WorkflowAgent.generate()` stops at the default limit.
- 7ce7ffc: fix(workflow): log provider warnings in `WorkflowAgent`

`WorkflowAgent.generate()` and `WorkflowAgent.stream()` now log the
warnings of every model call through the AI SDK warning logger, like
`ToolLoopAgent`. The `AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS` global controls the output.

- f6809e3: fix(workflow): align the `prepareStep` results of
`WorkflowAgent` with `ToolLoopAgent`. Returned `instructions` (or the
deprecated `system`) replace the instructions of the step and carry
forward to later steps, returned `providerOptions` are merged with the
agent options, and returned `headers` are merged over the headers of the
call.
- f1de9cb: feat(workflow): support the `timeout` object in
`WorkflowAgent`

`generate()` and `stream()` accept `timeout: { totalMs, stepMs,
firstChunkMs, chunkMs }` in addition to a number. `stepMs` limits each
model call. In `stream()`, `firstChunkMs` and `chunkMs` limit the wait
for model output. Invalid timeout values are rejected with an
`InvalidArgumentError`. A timeout now also ends a model step when the
provider stream ignores the abort signal.

## @ai-sdk/workflow@2.0.105

### Patch Changes

- ff89832: fix(workflow): call `onAbort` instead of `onError` when a
`WorkflowAgent` call is aborted during a model step with a custom abort
reason. `generate()` still rejects with that reason. `stream()` now
resolves with the steps that finished, as it does for an abort without a
reason.
- 2473a71: fix(workflow): `WorkflowAgent` uses the last value yielded by
an async generator tool as the tool result, like `ToolLoopAgent`. A
generator that throws after yielding produces a tool error.
- f43ee39: fix(workflow): log the default step limit warning when
`WorkflowAgent.generate()` stops at the default limit.
- 7ce7ffc: fix(workflow): log provider warnings in `WorkflowAgent`

`WorkflowAgent.generate()` and `WorkflowAgent.stream()` now log the
warnings of every model call through the AI SDK warning logger, like
`ToolLoopAgent`. The `AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS` global controls the output.

- f6809e3: fix(workflow): align the `prepareStep` results of
`WorkflowAgent` with `ToolLoopAgent`. Returned `instructions` (or the
deprecated `system`) replace the instructions of the step and carry
forward to later steps, returned `providerOptions` are merged with the
agent options, and returned `headers` are merged over the headers of the
call.
- 9307549: feat(workflow): support `experimental_refineToolInput` in
`WorkflowAgent`, in the constructor and per call. Refined tool inputs
are used for tool execution, step results, callbacks, and the next model
call, like in `ToolLoopAgent`.
- bf1dd2a: fix(workflow): `WorkflowAgent.stream()` keeps the tool call
in the step result when the model calls an unknown tool or passes input
that does not match the schema. The call is marked `invalid` and the
step has a `tool-error` part, as in `generate()` and `ToolLoopAgent`.
The model still receives the error as a tool result.
- 453d880: fix(workflow): call the `onInputAvailable` tool hook in
`stream()` when the provider sends a tool call without streaming its
input first.
- 5c0e984: fix(workflow): report the provider name and model ID of the
called model in the steps of `WorkflowAgent.stream()` results, matching
`ToolLoopAgent` and `WorkflowAgent.generate()`
- b9f6c82: feat(workflow): support `toolOrder` in `WorkflowAgent`

`WorkflowAgent` accepts `toolOrder` in the constructor, per call in
`generate()` and `stream()`, and from `prepareCall` and `prepareStep`.
Listed tools are sent first in the listed order, and the remaining tools
follow in alphabetical order.

- f1de9cb: feat(workflow): support the `timeout` object in
`WorkflowAgent`

`generate()` and `stream()` accept `timeout: { totalMs, stepMs,
firstChunkMs, chunkMs }` in addition to a number. `stepMs` limits each
model call. In `stream()`, `firstChunkMs` and `chunkMs` limit the wait
for model output. Invalid timeout values are rejected with an
`InvalidArgumentError`. A timeout now also ends a model step when the
provider stream ignores the abort signal.

feat(heygen): add decision models (#25037)

## Background

HeyGen released [HeyGen
Decision](https://developers.heygen.com/docs/models/heygen-decision), a
decision API (`POST /v3/models/decisions`) that answers named yes/no
(`noul`), choice, and score questions about text, images, and video with
probabilities. Its request and answer shapes closely match the existing
experimental decision models (Perplexity, TypeSafe), so `@ai-sdk/heygen`
can expose it through `experimental_decide`.

## Summary

- Add `heygen.decisionModel(modelId)` returning an
`Experimental_DecisionModelV4` (`DecisionHeyGenModel`), with
`heygen-decision-1` and `heygen-decision-1-turbo` in the model catalog.
Other model IDs are passed through unchanged.
- Map SDK `boolean` questions to HeyGen `noul`, and `noul` answers back
to `probability`. Choice and Score distributions are returned at full
precision. Box questions are rejected as unsupported.
- Send image and video file parts as HeyGen `assets.images` /
`assets.videos` (inline data as base64, HTTPS URLs as `url`, `{ heygen:
assetId }` provider references as `asset_id`), keeping text and JSON
parts in `state`.
- Validate HeyGen's documented limits before I/O: 1–400 questions with
valid names (nonempty, no colon or newline, no surrounding whitespace),
1–255 choice options, 1–10 non-null score levels, at most 4 images and 1
video.
- Unwrap HeyGen's `data` envelope. Expose `confidence`, `legend`,
per-answer `answerWarnings`, and `requestId` in
`providerMetadata.heygen`. Use the decision `id` as `response.id`, and
preserve usage.
- `maxOutputTokens`, `reasoning`, and `providerOptions.heygen.*` produce
unsupported warnings and are not sent.
- Docs: HeyGen provider page (Decision Models section and generated
capability table), the decisions guide provider table, and the package
README. Examples:
`examples/ai-functions/src/decide/heygen/{basic,video}.ts`.

## End-to-End Verification

Built this checkout's packages (`pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai...
--filter=@ai-sdk/heygen...`) and ran against the live HeyGen API with a
HeyGen API key in `HEYGEN_API_KEY`. Scripts ran from
`examples/ai-functions`, so `ai` and `@ai-sdk/heygen` resolved to the
workspace packages.

```bash
cd examples/ai-functions
pnpm tsx src/decide/heygen/basic.ts
pnpm tsx src/decide/heygen/video.ts
```

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `heygen-decision-1`, text with boolean, choice, and score questions,
via `experimental_decide` | Answers passed core validation; `team:
video` (p≈0.994), `blocked` p≈0.88, `impact` score ≈1.99; 863 input
tokens; confidence, legend, request ID, and decision ID populated |
| `heygen-decision-1-turbo`, same request | Same answer shapes; 632
input tokens |
| PNG bytes plus JSON state, via `experimental_decide` | Sent as
`assets.images.image-1` (base64); `animal: cat` (p≈0.999) |
| HTTPS image URL, via `doDecide` | Sent as a `url` asset; answered |
| MP4 bytes, via `experimental_decide` (`video.ts`) | Sent as
`assets.videos.video-1` (base64); answered; 5,036 input tokens |
| Unknown model ID | `APICallError` 400: `Input should be
'heygen-decision-1' or 'heygen-decision-1-turbo' (invalid_parameter)
[model]` |

The live response matched the adapter's schema (`data.id`,
`data.request_id`, `data.model`, `data.answers`, `data.usage`).
Probabilities are returned at full precision, so no `rounding` is
declared.

Not verified live: uploaded-asset (`asset_id`) inputs and per-answer
`warning` values; both are covered by unit tests.

fix(ai): prevent repeated UI validation error amplification (#24906)

## Background

Repeated malformed UI message parts cause Core validation to accumulate
the full part-union error tree for every part before agent execution. A
7,550-byte input on current `main` produced a 53,898,977-byte exception.

## Summary

Stop structural validation at the first invalid element in message,
part, and steering-part arrays. Select the applicable part type and tool
state before validating fields, preventing malformed metadata from
multiplying across unrelated alternatives. Preserve the first error's
path and existing `TypeValidationError` shape, and continue accepting
large valid arrays. Add regression coverage, document the diagnostic
behavior, and add an `ai` patch changeset.

This is a Core UI validation issue shared by all providers.
`packages/ai/src/ui/validate-ui-messages.ts` changes the structural
validator; its tests and
`src/agent/create-agent-ui-stream-response.test.ts` cover rejection
before agent execution. `packages/provider/` and
`packages/provider-utils/` are unchanged. No API signature or count
limit is introduced. Error diagnostics report the first structural
failure; sharing tool schemas can change validated tool-object key order
while preserving their fields and values.

## Contributor Credit

Thanks to 0x4ym3n for the report and reproduction in HackerOne report
4142373.

before and after the fix using rebuilt local workspace packages. It
measures exception amplification and verifies that malformed input is
rejected before the agent runs.

including implementation and verification details. The [follow-up
discussion](https://vercel.slack.com/archives/C050WU03V3N/p1794507950779149?thread_ts=1794507126.136719&cid=C050WU03V3N)

preview](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/codex/simplify-adr-format/skills/adr-skill/assets/templates/adr-simple.md)
👀

- Reformat the tool-error ADR around context, decision, alternatives,
and references. Preserve the decision details and relevant reasoning,
fold unique consequences into the option comparison, and link #24980 for
implementation and verification.
- Use a single simple ADR template: remove the redundant MADR template
and template-selection guide, along with YAML frontmatter, separate
consequences, implementation plans, and verification sections. Omit
explicit status fields: merging the pull request accepts the decision.
- Align the ADR skill, review checklist, examples, index guidance, and
generators with the concise format. Remove template selection, unused
metadata options, generated status metadata, and the obsolete status
helper. Add a dated format amendment to the original ADR adoption
record.

affecting multiple layers. Require consent before unsolicited ADR
creation or edits, and enforce date-prefixed filenames in both
generators.

fix(amazon-bedrock): stop renaming thinking block_binding field (#24919)

## Background

- in #20728, we renamed
`thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to just
`mismatch_behavior` for Bedrock Anthropic requests
- at the time, some AWS regions (`us-east-1`) aliased
`prefix_mismatch_behavior` to `mismatch_behavior` automatically. but
other AWS regions (`eu-central-1`) didn't, and rejected the request.
- this has since changed; AWS accepts `prefix_mismatch_behavior` now in
all tested regions as the *actual* field, and
[documents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-thinking-block-binding.html#claude-messages-thinking-block-binding-request-object)
`mismatch_behavior` as a deprecated alias

## Summary

stop renaming `block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` in the Bedrock
Anthropic provider

## End-to-End Verification

checked the combo of:
- a bunch of different AWS regions: us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1,
us-west-2, ca-central-1, sa-east-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2,
eu-west-3, eu-north-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-northeast-2, ap-northeast-3,
ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1 and ap-southeast-2
- a bunch of different claude models: haiku-5-5, sonnet-5, sonnet-5-5,
sonnet-4-6, opus-5, opus-5-5, opus-4-8, opus-4-7 and opus-4-6.

fix(google): support top-level reasoning in iAPI (#25035)

## Background

https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/24983

Google’s standard Generate Content adapter supports portable top-level
reasoning, but google.interactions(...) silently ignored it for both
generation and streaming. Interactions only forwarded
providerOptions.google.thinkingLevel.

Consequently, passing reasoning: 'xhigh' to Gemini 4 Hydrogen left
thinking depth at the API default instead of requesting its highest
reasoning level

## Summary

- Map reasoning to generation_config.thinking_level using the model
catalog and existing reasoning mapper
- Preserve explicit thinkingLevel overrides and API defaults; warn for
unsupported levels and agent calls
